phase: Pocket-traversal redesign. Stop placing the tunnel in microscopic system-space; make it its own human-scale pocket (~60u) the camera physically flies through (into Portal A, real interior, out Portal B). Real plane-crossings restore the entry/cruise/emergence choreography the 4285602 pin deleted. HYPER is load-adaptive: min-cruise + emergence gated on destination-ready. Reference impl: portal-traversal-lab.html. Design spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-06-warp-tunnel-pocket-traversal-design.md. Risk R1 (pocket rig <-> post-teleport world-coords reconciliation) resolved in the impl plan before TDD. [2026-06-07 amendment] Live diagnosis (Sol->Shudpis, GPU 9223) showed the arrival 'freeze/teleport/disappear' = (a) a 324ms first-render shader-compile hitch at the swap, (b) an OCCLUDED ~3150u teleport (mode=INSIDE, tunnel visible throughout), (c) the tunnel force-hidden + a FORCED INSIDE->OUTSIDE_B flip at onComplete (no real crossing) + a per-frame portal-follow dragging the ring 60u behind the camera. 'Approach C' (the no-teleport rebase inversion) was found UNNECESSARY: the teleport is never visible and the freeze is shader-compile (identical cost teleport-or-rebase). Scope = the existing Tasks 4-7 emergence + arrival polish: AC7 stationary portal, AC8 close-tween, AC9 no-freeze (shader pre-compile in HYPER), AC10 swap-occlusion invariant guard. Tasks 0-3 (entry, Fix D) unchanged, pending Max UAT.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every warp renders the tunnel during HYPER with no black screen, including repeat warps in the same session and warps to far targets.

verifyVia.input: Drive a chain of warps from Sol via _autoSelectWarpTarget() -> _beginWarpTurn(), including >=2 consecutive repeat warps (window.__wd.runRepeatWarpSuite()) and a far target; sample per HYPER frame.
verifyVia.observable: On 10/10 warps, takeSceneInventory().meshes[name=='effect.warp.tunnel'] is present and inFrustum on every HYPER frame and portal mode reaches INSIDE during HYPER; zero black-HYPER frames across all runs (multi-run gate, not single-pass).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every warp flies INTO Portal A: the traversal goes OUTSIDE_A -> INSIDE via a real plane crossing, reached from OUTSIDE_A by the camera crossing the portal plane — not by a forced setTraversalMode('INSIDE').

verifyVia.input: Headless test (in tests/warp-tunnel-rebase.test.js, replacing the retired pin-invariant tests): construct the pocket rig + a synthetic camera at the OUTSIDE_A side and advance it forward along the pocket axis through Portal A's plane, calling WarpPortal.updateTraversal(camera) each step.
verifyVia.observable: Traversal mode transitions OUTSIDE_A -> INSIDE; insideAt is recorded by updateTraversal (the plane-crossing path), and the transition is NOT produced by a forced setTraversalMode call.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: During HYPER the camera physically advances forward through the pocket interior, facing forward — it reads as travelling a real interior, never looking backward.

verifyVia.input: Drive a live warp (chrome-devtools GPU 9223); sample the camera position projected onto the pocket axis and the camera forward vector each HYPER frame.
verifyVia.observable: Axis-distance travelled increases monotonically across the HYPER window (real forward travel, not static texture-scroll); camera-forward dotted with the pocket axis stays positive throughout (no backward orientation).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every warp emerges OUT through Portal B: the traversal goes INSIDE -> OUTSIDE_B via a real plane crossing, occurring BEFORE the EXIT phase completes — not a snap at onComplete.

verifyVia.input: Headless test (same suite, continuation of AC2): keep advancing the synthetic camera through the pocket past Portal B's plane, calling updateTraversal each step.
verifyVia.observable: Traversal mode transitions INSIDE -> OUTSIDE_B; outsideBAt is recorded via the plane-crossing path, and the transition occurs before the EXIT-complete / onComplete callback fires (not coincident with it).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A slow background load extends the cruise rather than emerging into a half-loaded system: emergence is withheld until destination-ready is true, while a minimum cruise time is always honored.

verifyVia.input: Headless test: run the HYPER timing/gate logic with a stubbed destination-ready signal that resolves AFTER the minimum cruise time, and a control case where it resolves before.
verifyVia.observable: Emergence (reaching Portal B / mode flip to OUTSIDE_B) does not occur until the ready flag is set: with a late-resolving stub the cruise duration extends past the minimum until ready; with an early-resolving stub the cruise lasts exactly the minimum. Min-cruise is never violated.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Riding the warp, the whole thing reads as into-hole -> travel -> out-of-hole: head-on approach into Portal A, a cruise that feels long, emergence out Portal B into the new system; the tunnel and portal ring sit STILL behind me and close over a few seconds as I fly away — if I turn and look back during exit I see them closing, not already gone — and nothing freezes, looks-backward, or snaps.

verifyVia.input: Max rides several warps in the running game — including repeats in one session and jumps to distant targets — watching each phase, and freelooking behind on exit at least once.
verifyVia.observable: Holistic acceptance — the warp feels like flying into and out of a hole in space, the cruise reads as long, the portal sits still behind me and closes as I coast into the new system, nothing looks backward / freezes / snaps. Deferred to Max.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: On arrival the tunnel and portal ring stay STILL at the exit point in world space — they do NOT follow / re-pin behind the moving camera. As the camera coasts into the new system the portal falls behind it (Symptom A fixed: the per-frame follow-reposition is removed).

verifyVia.input: Drive a live warp (chrome-devtools GPU 9223); after the INSIDE->OUTSIDE_B emergence crossing, sample the warpPortal group's world-true position (group.position + worldOrigin) and the camera each frame for ~3s as the camera coasts away.
verifyVia.observable: The portal group's world-true position stays constant (within rebase tolerance) across the coast — NOT held at a fixed camera-relative offset; camera->portal distance increases monotonically; camera-forward . (portal - camera) goes negative (the portal ends up behind the camera). The per-frame follow-reposition code path no longer runs.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Starting at the emergence crossing, the tunnel + portal ring close — shrink and fade — over ~3s, then disappear; the tunnel stays VISIBLE the whole time it is closing, so a look-back during exit shows it closing rather than already gone.

verifyVia.input: Live warp; from the INSIDE->OUTSIDE_B crossing, sample portal radius (WarpPortal._radius), rim intensity, tunnel material opacity, and _tunnel.visible each frame until the portal closes. (Tween driver math also unit-tested headless via the makeFakePortal .call() pattern.)
verifyVia.observable: radius, rim intensity, and tunnel opacity decrease monotonically to ~0 over ~3s; _tunnel.visible remains true throughout the close and only becomes false when the tween completes (close()) — NOT force-hidden at the instant of the mode flip.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The arrival does not freeze: the first-render cost of the new system (shader/material compilation + GPU upload) is pre-paid during HYPER, so no long frame lands at or after the system swap. (Baseline 2026-06-07: a 324ms frame on the first render of the spawned system — this AC eliminates it.)

verifyVia.input: Live warp with a per-frame dt sampler across the swap + emergence window (the onSwapSystem frame through the first ~30 frames after); compare to the median in-warp frame time.
verifyVia.observable: No frame in the swap->emergence window exceeds ~50ms (about 3 dropped frames at 60fps); specifically the first-render-after-spawn frame is under the threshold. Destination-system shader programs are compiled before the reveal (e.g. renderer.compileAsync during HYPER), not on the first visible frame.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Regression guard (protects future camera/movement changes): the system swap + camera teleport ONLY ever happens while the camera is INSIDE the tunnel with the tunnel occluding the forward view, so the ~3000u teleport is never visible. If a future change exposes it, this fails loudly.

verifyVia.input: Live warp; at the onSwapSystem callback frame, capture traversalMode, _tunnel.visible, and the camera's position relative to the tunnel interior bounds. (Also assertable headless as a timing invariant if the swap trigger logic is pure.)
verifyVia.observable: At the swap frame: traversalMode === 'INSIDE' AND _tunnel.visible === true AND the camera is within the tunnel interior (walls between camera and the destination scene). The swap never fires during OUTSIDE_A / OUTSIDE_B or with the tunnel hidden.
